newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Polar appliance firm plans 1997 flotation.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Polar appliance firm plans 1997 flotation.

text.p: Poland's white goods maker Polar SA plans to offer more than 70 million zlotys worth of new stock to the public and to enter the Warsaw bourse in the first half of 1997, the company's president said on Tuesday.

Zbigniew Szczypinski told Reuters the state-owned company based in the western city of Wroclaw wanted to issue new shares to boost its capital and to finance its 70 million zloty investment programme. @
"We want to go public and raise capital...we would also like to enter the stock exchange and we want this to happen towards the end of the first half of 1997," Szczypinski said.
He said an issue prospectus should be ready by the end of this year. He did not say whether the treasury, which now owns the company, would float existing shares simultaneously with the new offering.

Szczypinski said the company, which makes refrigerators, freezers and washing machines, would not seek a strategic investor in the near future but did not rule out an alliance with another renowned producer later. @

"We don't think about a strategic investor right now but competition is likely to force us to seek a stronger partner...but we would want to discuss it (strategic partnership) as a privatised company," Szczypinski said.

Polar's marketing director Andrzej Krowinski, also present, told reporters the company aimed to boost next year its share of the Polish appliances market to 60 percent from the present 45 percent by refining and expanding its product range. @
"We want to achieve that by launching new products, we have already started introduced air conditioners and we plan next year to launch dishwashing machines and microwave ovens," Krowinski said.
Szczypinski said Polar had a pre-tax profit of eight million zlotys on sales of 330 million in the first eight months of this year up from a three-million zloty pre-tax for the whole of 1995.
